result: The study surveyed microbiota from 159 individuals across 60 families with varying compositions (children, dogs, both, or neither), sampling fecal, oral, and skin sites from humans and dogs. DNA was extracted, 16S rRNA V2 region amplified, and sequenced using Illumina GAIIx, yielding 969 samples with 74,855,127 total reads after quality filtering.

result: Household members, particularly couples, shared more microbiota than individuals from different households, with stronger effects on skin than oral or fecal sites. Family membership explained a large proportion of variability in bacterial diversity across all body sites, with partner comparisons showing the strongest effects (R < 0.30 for tongue/feces).
